newsitem.title: USA: Firmer NYMEX helps offset lower spot product diffs.
newsitem.headline: Firmer NYMEX helps offset lower spot product diffs.

text.p: Firmer NYMEX futures helped offset mostly lower differentials on U.S. spot products late Wednesday, with U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded gasoline sagging on lackluster buying interest, players said.

NYMEX April gasoline moved out of earlier negative territory to settle 0.48 cent higher while April heat eked out a 0.11 cent gain after new EIA and API data showing sizeable draws on gasoline and distillate stocks last week.
Barrels of "M4" winter-grade gasoline went begging in New York Harbor, keeping differentials mired at about 5.0 cents below April futures, stable with Tuesday.
Traders said "M4," with its more-volatile 13.5 lb Reid Vapor Pressure, was finding few takers because of the imminent switchover to 9-lb "M2" spring gasoline grades.
They said the market was preparing for April 1, when the Buckeye Pipeline serving upstate New York and Pennsylvania will only ship lower-vapor-pressure grades.
NYH "M2" grade, meanwhile, was offered at about 2.0 cents below the print, while Gulf Coast "M2" conventional unleaded saw diffs ease 0.50 cent to 4.30 cents below the print.
